Base directory for this skill: /tmp/fceval-a3-t2-fdzbp934/cfg/skills/firecrawl

# Firecrawl CLI

Search, scrape, and interact with the web. Returns clean markdown optimized for LLM context windows.

Run `firecrawl --help` or `firecrawl <command> --help` for full option details. For app integration or outcome workflows (research briefs, SEO audits, etc.), route to the `firecrawl-build` / `firecrawl-workflows` skills — see [When to Load References](#when-to-load-references).

## Prerequisites

Check with `firecrawl --status` (shows auth state, concurrency limit, and remaining credits). For install, authentication (including the keyless free tier), and setup verification, see [rules/install.md](rules/install.md). For output handling guidelines, see [rules/security.md](rules/security.md).

## Workflow

Use Firecrawl for anything that needs the internet (searching, reading pages, URLs, raw files or JSON APIs, GitHub, docs, papers) instead of WebSearch, WebFetch, curl or wget, even when the task doesn't name Firecrawl. Local documents (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX) go to `parse`.

**Freshness:** `scrape` serves cached content up to 2 days old by default. Add `--max-age 0` for anything that changes often: latest versions, releases, PR or issue state, prices, status pages, live JSON APIs.

For structured datasets, first check for a suitable workflow or data provider using the [search skill](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md). Read a known page directly; reuse a selected contract instead of repeating discovery.

Follow this escalation pattern:

1. **Search** - Start with the actual question: `developer` for code questions, `research` for papers, otherwise `search`. Find web sources and relevant structured-data tools through semantic and domain matching.
2. **Inspect + Scrape** - For a tool match, use `list <provider> <capability> --pretty` if its contract is missing, then execute with `scrape <provider/capability> --options '<JSON>'`. For a URL, scrape its content directly.
3. **Map + Scrape** - Large site or need a specific subpage. Use `map --search` to find the right URL, then scrape it.
4. **Crawl** - Need bulk content from an entire site section (e.g., all /docs/).
5. **Monitor** - Need recurring checks or ongoing alerts. Prefer setting a monitor with `--page` plus `--goal` instead of doing repeated one-off scrapes.
6. **Interact** - Scrape first, then interact with the page (pagination, modals, form submissions, multi-step navigation).

| Need                        | Command               | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find pages on a topic       | `search`              | No specific URL yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Find research papers        | `research`            | Biomedical/clinical/scientific literature — use the paper index                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Answer a coding question    | `developer`           | Issues, merged PRs, READMEs, and docs — not a general web page                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Find US law or regulation   | `gov`                 | US statutes, regulations, codes, and court opinions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Get a page's content        | `scrape`              | Have a URL: HTML, JS-rendered, raw file or JSON API (instead of curl/wget; `--max-age 0` for live data)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Find URLs within a site     | `map`                 | Know the site but not the page: `map <url> --search "<topic>"` ranks that site's URLs (fast, 1 credit), then scrape the top match. Use instead of guessing URLs. May miss pages: use `crawl` for a complete list, `scrape --format links` for links on one page                                                                                         |
| Bulk extract a site section | `crawl`               | Many pages of one site or section ("every page under /docs", "first N pages"). Use instead of scraping pages one by one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| AI-powered data extraction  | `agent`               | Pages unknown, or many records across sites (directories, listings, "find N companies that…"). Not for one known URL or one search                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Interact with a page        | `scrape` + `interact` | Data appears only after actions on the page (log in, type into a search box or form, click tabs/"load more", paginate): scrape the URL first, then `firecrawl interact "<one small task>"` per step, and `firecrawl interact stop` when done (billed per minute). Use `--profile` to stay logged in. Not needed if plain scrape already has the content |
| Download a site to files    | `x download`          | Save an entire site as local files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Parse a local file          | `parse`               | File on disk (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, etc.) — not a URL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Watch pages for changes     | `monitor`             | Schedule recurring scrapes/crawls, diff against snapshots                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

For detailed command reference, run `firecrawl <command> --help`.

For US legal or regulatory source discovery, start with `firecrawl gov "<question, jurisdiction, and date>" --limit 10`. If the user supplies a source URL, read it directly with `scrape`. Results are excerpts, not a guarantee of official-only sources or current governing law: verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing a controlling section and supporting passage. Ask for a missing jurisdiction before identifying the governing rule. Use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage; no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists.

**Done when:** the narrowest suitable command has completed the request, its output was inspected, and the answer cites the saved source files.

**Scrape vs interact:**

- Use `scrape` first. It handles static pages and JS-rendered SPAs.
- Use `scrape` + `interact` when you need to interact with a page, such as clicking buttons, filling out forms, navigating through a complex site, infinite scroll, or when scrape fails to grab all the content you need.
- For web searches, use `search` — interact is for acting on a specific page.

**Monitor:** Bias toward `monitor` when the user's goal is ongoing change detection, alerting, or repeated checks over time — not another one-off scrape. Goal writing, schedules, target modes, and JSON-mode change tracking are documented in [firecrawl-monitor](../firecrawl-monitor/SKILL.md).

**Reuse fetched content:**

- `search --scrape` already fetches full page content. Reuse it instead of re-scraping those URLs.
- Check `.firecrawl/` for existing data before fetching again.

## Large results and Alexandria

`search` discovers web results and tools, `list` reveals a selected tool's contract, and `scrape <provider/capability> --options '<JSON>'` executes it. Inspect only the contracts needed for the task.

A client context/output error does not prove the provider failed. Keep the request/scrape ID and inspect saved output or use `scrape firecrawl/bash` against the retained result before repeating the request. See [large-result recovery](../firecrawl-scrape/references/large-results.md). Do not assume the client can signal an overflow back to the tool, or that Bash supports search IDs or every provider's retained data.

## When to Load References

- **Searching the web or finding sources first** -> [firecrawl-search](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md)
- **Finding research papers (biomedical, clinical, or scientific literature; PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv)** -> [firecrawl-research-index](../firecrawl-research-index/SKILL.md). Use the paper index instead of scraping PubMed or Google Scholar by hand; `search --categories research` is a website filter, not the paper index.
- **Answering a library, API, error, or known-bug question from issues, merged PRs, READMEs, or docs** -> [firecrawl-developer-index](../firecrawl-developer-index/SKILL.md)
- **Scraping a known URL** -> [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md)
- **Finding URLs on a known site** -> [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md)
- **Bulk extraction from a docs section or site** -> [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md)
- **AI-powered structured extraction from complex sites** -> [firecrawl-agent](../firecrawl-agent/SKILL.md)
- **Clicks, forms, login, pagination, or post-scrape browser actions** -> [firecrawl-interact](../firecrawl-interact/SKILL.md)
- **Downloading a site to local files** -> [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md)
- **Parsing a local file (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, HTML, etc.)** -> [firecrawl-parse](../firecrawl-parse/SKILL.md)
- **Detecting content changes on a website and getting notified by webhook or email (pricing, jobs, posts, docs, status pages, anything ongoing)** -> [firecrawl-monitor](../firecrawl-monitor/SKILL.md)
- **Install, auth, or setup problems** -> [rules/install.md](rules/install.md)
- **Output handling and safe file-reading patterns** -> [rules/security.md](rules/security.md)
- **Integrating Firecrawl into an app, adding `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` to `.env`, or choosing endpoint usage in product code** -> the [firecrawl-build skills](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build) (`firecrawl-build-onboarding`, `-scrape`, `-search`, `-interact`). They live in a separate repo; install with `firecrawl setup build`.
- **Producing Firecrawl-powered deliverables such as research briefs, SEO audits, QA reports, lead lists, knowledge bases, or design-system extraction** -> use the `firecrawl-workflows` skills (already installed alongside this CLI skill). These skills infer from context first and ask only short blocking questions when needed.

## Output & Organization

Unless the user specifies to return in context, write results to `.firecrawl/` with `-o`. Add `.firecrawl/` to `.gitignore`. Always quote URLs - shell interprets `?` and `&` as special characters.

```bash
firecrawl search "react hooks" -o .firecrawl/search-react-hooks.json --json
firecrawl scrape "<url>" -o .firecrawl/page.md
```

Naming conventions:

```
.firecrawl/search-{query}.json
.firecrawl/search-{query}-scraped.json
.firecrawl/{site}-{path}.md
```

Read output files incrementally with `grep`, `head`, or bounded reads:

```bash
wc -l .firecrawl/file.md && head -50 .firecrawl/file.md
grep -n "keyword" .firecrawl/file.md
```

Single format outputs raw content. Multiple formats (e.g., `--format markdown,links`) output JSON. Use `jq` to work with JSON output, e.g. `jq -r '.data.web[].url' .firecrawl/search.json`.

## Feedback

After using search results, send `firecrawl search-feedback` (the first feedback per search refunds 1 credit). The full pattern, guard, and rules live in [firecrawl-search](../firecrawl-search/SKILL.md).

For Alexandria feedback about a provider result or coverage gap (each refunds 1 credit, up to 10 per website and 100 per team each UTC day), see [firecrawl-alexandria](../firecrawl-alexandria/SKILL.md).

For non-search endpoint jobs, use `firecrawl feedback <endpoint> <jobId>` to send concise job-level feedback through `/v2/feedback`. Supported endpoints are `search`, `scrape`, `parse`, and `map`.

```bash
firecrawl feedback scrape "$SCRAPE_ID" \
  --rating partial \
  --issues missing_markdown \
  --tags docs \
  --note "The pricing table was missing from the markdown output." \
  --url "https://example.com/pricing" \
  --page-numbers 1 \
  --silent &
```

Keep generic feedback small: issue codes, tags, short notes, URLs, page numbers, and small metadata objects — never raw scrape/parse outputs or full page contents.

**Opt out:** `export FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1` makes the CLI skip every endpoint feedback call silently. Respect that flag — do not try to work around it.

## Parallelization

Run independent operations in parallel. Check `firecrawl --status` for concurrency limit:

```bash
firecrawl scrape "<url-1>" -o .firecrawl/1.md &
firecrawl scrape "<url-2>" -o .firecrawl/2.md &
firecrawl scrape "<url-3>" -o .firecrawl/3.md &
wait
```

For interact, scrape multiple pages and interact with each independently using their scrape IDs.

## Credit Usage

```bash
firecrawl credit-usage
firecrawl credit-usage --json --pretty -o .firecrawl/credits.json
```

# [Office Of The Registrar](https://cost.illinois.edu/)
## Primary Menu
- [Calculate Cost](https://cost.illinois.edu/)
- [Aid & Scholarships](http://osfa.illinois.edu/)
- [Cost Details](https://registrar.illinois.edu/tuition-fees/)
- [Bill Pay](https://paymybill.uillinois.edu/)
- [Contact Us](mailto:registration@illinois.edu)
# 2026 - 2027 Undergrad Base Tuition Rates
The base rate applies to the following colleges and majors. Tuition and fees are direct costs charged by the university. The cost of attendance also includes indirect cost allowances for food, housing, books, supplies and other expenses.  You will not be billed by the university for these costs unl
- **Applied Health Sciences:** All majors except Kinesiology
- **Education:** All majors except Computer Science & Education
- _**Division of Exploratory Studies:** All majors_
- _**Agricultural, Consumer, & Environmental Sciences (ACES):**_
_- Agricultural Leadership, Education & Communications_
_- Human Development & Family Studies_
_- Sustainability in Food & Environmental Sciences_
- _**Liberal Arts and Sciences:** All majors except:_
  - _Astrophysics (admitted Summer 2025 or after)_\\*\\*\\* See Base Rate if admitted before Summer 2025
  - Chemistry & Life Sciences majors: Biochemistry, Chemistry, Biology, Integrative Biology, Molecular & Cellular Biology, Molecular & Cellular Biology + Data Science and Neuroscience
  - Economics related majors: Economics and Econometrics & Quantitative Economics
  - Engineering-related majors:
    - Chemical Engineering
    - Chemical Engineering + Data Science
    - Mathematics & Computer Science\*
    - Statistics & Computer Science\*
    - Computer Science & Anthropology
    - Computer Science & Astronomy\*
    - Computer Science & Chemistry\*
    - Computer Science & Economics\*
    - Computer Science and Geography/Geographic Information Science
    - Computer Science & Linguistics\*
    - Computer Science & Philosophy\*
    - Statistics & Computer Science
  - **School of Social Work:** All majors
Non-degree students in these colleges are charged the non-guaranteed rate in the before Summer 2020 section.
_\\* Denotes a combined program_
## Other Notes
### Additional Course-Based Tuition
Students who enter the university Fall 2011 or later and take MCB 250, 251, 252, 253, or 450 are responsible for additional course-based tuition of $320 per course unless they are already paying differential tuition during the term of course enrollment.
### LAS International Rate
The LAS International rate applies to international students in the College of Liberal Arts & Sciences who are not already paying a program specific international differential.
## Academic Year Rates
| Entry Term | Resident Rate | Nonresident Rate | LAS International Rate | Other International Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Summer 2026 through Spring 2027 (guaranteed rate) | $13,252.00 | $35,928.00 | $38,576.00 | $36,970.00 |
| Summer 2025 through Spring 2026 (guaranteed rate) | $12,992.00 | $33,344.00 | $35,872.00 | $34,338.00 |

These are the charges you can expect to see on your tuition bill. Understanding your total estimated costs now can help you plan ahead and budget confidently. After you apply, you'll be able to see how our various financial aid options help cover expenses and help make Northwestern affordable for ev
For a full estimate of all static and incidental costs, see [Cost of Attendance](https://undergradaid.northwestern.edu/how-aid-works/cost-of-attendance/index.html). Keep in mind, you may encounter additional possible charges, such as late fees, depending on your program. For the billing schedule, se
If you have questions about tuition, fees or your bill, please visit our [FAQ page](https://www.northwestern.edu/sfs/faqs/index.html). View [tuition and fees from previous years](https://www.northwestern.edu/sfs/tuition/undergraduate/tuition-archive/index.html).
## Undergraduates
### Full-time Tuition$23,934/quarter
- All undergraduate students in degree programs must conform to the [Undergraduate Registration Requirement](https://www.registrar.northwestern.edu/registration-graduation/graduation-preparation/undergraduate-registration-requirements.html) (URR).
- Full-time registration for all undergraduate degree-seeking students is 3 to 5.5 units/quarter.
- Tuition is billed on the first invoice for each quarter.
### Part-time and Excess Course Tuition$8,517/unit
- Adjustments to tuition based on enrollment will be made after the last day to drop a class. See the [Academic Calendar](https://www.registrar.northwestern.edu/calendars/academic-calendars/)
- Part-time is fewer than 3 units/quarter
  - To be eligible for the part-time rate, a student must be enrolled in fewer than 3 units as of the last day for tuition adjustment for that term, see the [Academic Calendar](https://www.registrar.northwestern.edu/calendars/academic-calendars/) and review the [Policy on Dropping a Course](https://
  - _Note: **Most** financial aid programs require at least half-time enrollment; dropping below half-time may affect aid eligibility_
- Excess courses are more than 5.5 units/quarter
### Associated Student Government Fee$98/quarter
Covers special services and programs for students. Charged only in fall, winter, and spring quarters. For more ASG information, please visit [https://www.asg.northwestern.edu/](https://www.asg.northwestern.edu/)
### Athletics Event Fee$72/year
This fee allows undergraduate students to be admitted without charge to all of Northwestern's home athletic events, including football and basketball games. For more student athletic information, please visit: [https://nusports.com/sports/](https://nusports.com/)
### Student Health Fee$298/quarter
The Student Health Fee is paid in the fall, winter, and spring quarters. This fee, and other funding sources, provides Northwestern students with equitable access to a variety of health services at the university including: [Northwestern Medicine Student Health Service](https://www.northwestern.edu/
### NU-SHIP Annual PremiumVaries by coverage period (see below)
Undergraduate tuition will be $71,802; standard room and board will be $22,941; and fees will be $1,260.
The undergraduate student health and wellness, activity and athletics fees support a variety of services for students. The $894 student health and wellness fee goes toward student health and wellness programs, while the $294 activity fee supports student organizations and amenities. The $72 athletics fee allows undergraduates to attend all home athletics events.

# Undergraduate Tuition and Fees
Undergraduate tuition and fees are based on when a student began. There are two tuition types and each has three fee table options.
## Tuition Types
### Tuition Guarantee Cohorts
In 2017, the State of Ohio established the Ohio Tuition Guarantee. Undergraduate students that began summer 2017 or after are entered into a Tuition Guarantee Cohort. Tuition Guarantee Cohort students will use one of two tuition tables below:
[Undergraduate Fees - students that began summer 2026 or after](https://registrar.osu.edu/student-hub/tuition-and-fees/undergraduate-tuition-and-fees-2026-2027/undergraduate-fees-students-that-began-summer-2026-or-after-2026-2027/ "Undergraduate Fees - students that began summer 2026 or after")

- The Tuition Guarantee does not apply to the non-resident surcharge, international surcharge, or program/technology/course fees.
The Ohio State Tuition Guarantee applies to Ohio residents who are incoming first-year undergraduate students at each of Ohio State's campuses.
Ohio resident students who transfer to Ohio State will also join the guarantee program if they began their college career as a first-year student at another institution in autumn semester 2017 or later.

The following table shows the estimated expenses for the 2026-27 academic year for **first-year** undergraduate students at the University of Washington’s three campuses, as approved by the UW Board of Regents in June 2026. It reflects student fees and budgets for the regular academic year: fall, winter, and spring.
Note: the state’s allowable resident undergraduate tuition increase (under [RCW 28B.15.067](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=28B.15.067)) for the 2026-27 academic year is 3.3%. This is applicable only to resident undergraduate tuition. Non-resident, graduate, and fee-based program rates were also confirmed in June 2026. All rates are published on our [Current Tuition and Fees Dashboards](https://finance.uw.edu/tuition-fees/tuition/current-tuition-and-fees-dashboards "Current Tuitio
The Office of Student Financial Aid website has more information about [student budgets](https://www.washington.edu/financialaid/getting-started/student-budgets/), and other areas of the FPB website cover [student fees](https://finance.uw.edu/tuition-fees/fees/required-student-fees "Required Student Fees") and [annual tuition](https://finance.uw.edu/tuition-fees/tuition/current-tuition-and-fees-dashboards/annual-tuition-fees "Annual Tuition & Fees").

content.text:
Purdue is cheapest at $9,992 and USC is most expensive at $77,336. I read all 18 schools' own 2026-27 pages, between 10:00 and 19:10 on 2026-10-17. Northwestern and USC are private, so they charge everyone the same rate.

| 2 | Nebraska–Lincoln | $11,472 | Yes. The school's "Tuition & Fees" estimate assumes 15 credits a semester at $303 a credit. | https://admissions.unl.edu/cost/ and https://studentaccounts.unl.edu/tuition-and-fees/undergraduate-tuition-and-fees-2026-2027/ |

| 9 | UCLA | $16,430 | Yes ("University Fees", covering tuition and fees). Health insurance is extra. | https://admission.ucla.edu/tuition-aid/tuition-fees |

| 12 | Illinois (Urbana-Champaign, base rate) | $18,530 | Yes. See the note below. | https://www.admissions.illinois.edu/tuition/ and https://cost.illinois.edu/Home/UgradBase?DiffCode=BASE&TermCode=120268&TableType=1 |

| 15 | Rutgers (New Brunswick, Arts & Sciences) | $19,389 | Yes: $15,381 tuition plus $4,008 fees. | https://admissions.rutgers.edu/costs-and-aid/tuition-fees |
| 16 | Penn State (University Park, lower division) | $20,878 | Probably. See the note below. | https://tuition.psu.edu/rates-effective-2026-fall-semester |
| 17 | Northwestern | $73,062 | Yes: $71,802 tuition plus $1,260 fees. Health insurance is extra. | https://www.northwestern.edu/sfs/tuition/undergraduate/ |
| 18 | USC | $77,336 | Yes: $75,384 tuition plus $1,952 fees. New students also pay a $450 one-time fee, which makes $77,786 for a first-year. | https://financialaid.usc.edu/undergraduate-financial-aid/cost-of-attendance/ |

- **Illinois:** the school's own cost-of-attendance page gives a range of $18,530–$24,018 for tuition and fees. I took the low end as the base rate. It is consistent with the registrar's $13,252 base tuition, but I didn't find an itemized fee table to confirm it.
- **Penn State:** the page calls its rates "tuition and fees" but doesn't itemize them. I'm treating $20,878 as all-in, so the figure is less certain.
- **Credit loads:** Nebraska and Oregon bill by the credit, so their totals assume 15 credits a semester or term. Purdue, Maryland and Iowa use flat full-time rates. Wisconsin's figure is the published full-time rate.
- **Minnesota reciprocity:** I used the standard resident rate, not the reciprocity rate.
- **Program rates:** I used the general arts-and-sciences or base rate where schools charge more for engineering or business. Examples are Illinois, Michigan State, Minnesota and Maryland (for juniors and seniors).
